title: Israeli Drone Strike Kills 3 in Jenin as Defense Minister Declares Camp 'Permanently' Occupied
detail: On Friday, August 28, 2026, an Israeli drone struck a car in Jenin in the northern occupied West Bank, killing three Palestinians — Israel's first strike in the West Bank since February 2025. The military identified one of the dead as Qais Bitawi, described as a Hamas operative planning attacks, along with two others it called his accomplices; Palestinian Islamic Jihad said Bitawi was in fact a senior operative of its own armed wing, not Hamas. The Palestinian Red Crescent said Israeli troops detained medics at the scene and prevented casualties from being transported to hospital. Hours after the strike, Defense Minister Israel Katz declared that the Jenin refugee camp — emptied of its roughly 15,000 residents during the IDF's Operation Iron Wall invasion in early 2025 — is now 'permanently stationed' by Israeli forces, 'like other terrorist camps' in the West Bank, marking the first explicit Israeli declaration of indefinite military occupation of a depopulated West Bank refugee camp.

media.caption: Aftermath of the Israeli drone strike on a vehicle in Jenin, occupied West Bank, August 28, 2026

confidenceReason: Strike and casualty count confirmed directly by IDF statement and corroborated by Al Jazeera, Haaretz and Middle East Eye; Katz's 'permanently stationed' quote independently reported by Haaretz and Middle East Eye. The identity/affiliation of the named target is disputed between the IDF (Hamas) and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (its own operative).

title: Israeli Strikes Kill 5 Across Gaza, Including Three Members of Abdeen Family North of Khan Younis
detail: Early Friday morning, August 28, 2026, Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in three separate incidents across Gaza. A drone strike on a group of people north of Khan Younis in southern Gaza killed three members of the Abdeen family; their bodies were taken to Nasser Medical Complex. In Gaza City's Sabra neighborhood, a drone fired a missile at a group of civilians, killing a man identified by Palestinian sources as Hassan al-Deiri, whose body was taken to al-Shifa Hospital — the IDF separately said it had killed a Hamas sniper it named as Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri, along with a Hamas company commander, Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum, in northern Gaza operations the same day, alleging both were involved in weapons trafficking and 'advancing attacks on troops and civilians.' A third strike hit a displaced-persons tent in the Mashahra area east of Gaza City, killing one more person and wounding several others. The strikes came alongside the Jenin killings in the West Bank the same day and as UN data showed 46% of surveyed Gaza residents reported going to bed hungry at least once in the previous month, despite the October 2025 ceasefire.

media.caption: Aftermath of an Israeli strike in Gaza, August 28, 2026

confidenceReason: Casualty count and locations corroborated by Al Jazeera, a Times of Israel liveblog and Asharq Al-Awsat wire reporting citing Gaza health officials; the IDF's named-operative claims for the Sabra/northern Gaza dead have not been independently verified against the Palestinian-reported identity of Hassan al-Deiri, so that specific attribution carries lower certainty than the overall casualty count.
